title: Dengue deaths reach 458 as admissions stay high into November
excerpt: More than 1,600 people were admitted in a single day, most of them outside Dhaka division. October was the deadliest month so far.
content:
Three more people died of dengue and 1,674 were admitted to hospital in the 24 hours to 8am on 7 November, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), bdnews24.com and The Daily Star reported. This year’s death toll now stands at 458.

The numbers

  • Admissions in 2026: 147,580. Of these, 141,296 have been discharged and 5,826 are still in hospital.
  • Deaths by month: 148 in September, 174 in October, and 39 in the first seven days of November.
  • Where: of the latest day’s admissions, 714 were in Dhaka division and 960 elsewhere, led by Chattogram (311), Barishal (213) and Khulna (190).
  • Comparison: last year Bangladesh recorded more than 400 deaths and over 102,000 cases. The worst year on record, 2023, saw 321,179 admissions and 1,705 deaths.

Why it matters

Dengue is no longer a Dhaka problem. Most admissions now come from other divisions, where hospitals have fewer beds and less experience with severe cases. Health experts quoted by Reuters at the end of October said the threat was unlikely to ease before December. NGOs with community health workers can help with clean-up of breeding sites, early referral of high-risk patients and awareness in districts outside Dhaka.

What to watch

Whether November deaths overtake October’s, and the spread of cases in Chattogram, Barishal and Khulna divisions.
